description: The plot illustrates the relationship between Initial Confidence and three accuracy metrics: Final Accuracy, Δ Accuracy, and Initial Accuracy. The x-axis represents Initial Confidence, with a linear scale ranging from 0.81 to 0.99, and tick labels at intervals of 0.01. The y-axis represents Accuracy, with a linear scale ranging from 0.0 to 1.0, and tick labels at intervals of 0.2. The plot displays three lines: Final Accuracy in blue with a solid line style, Δ Accuracy in orange with a dashed line style, and Initial Accuracy in green with a dash-dot line style. The blue line for Final Accuracy remains relatively stable, starting at approximately 0.95 at an Initial Confidence of 0.81 and ending at around 0.94 at an Initial Confidence of 0.99, with some minor fluctuations. The orange line for Δ Accuracy starts at around 0.45 at an Initial Confidence of 0.81, decreases to approximately 0.1 at an Initial Confidence of 0.99, with some fluctuations in between, including a notable dip to around 0.2 at an Initial Confidence of 0.87. The green line for Initial Accuracy begins at approximately 0.5 at an Initial Confidence of 0.81, increases to around 0.8 at an Initial Confidence of 0.99, with some fluctuations, including a peak of around 0.7 at an Initial Confidence of 0.86 and a slight dip to around 0.6 at an Initial Confidence of 0.90. All three lines have error bars indicating the range of values.
